accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the zonal system under the 1975 Order in undivided Andhra Pradesh:
1. Zones I to III comprised Coastal Andhra.
2. Zone IV comprised Rayalaseema.
3. Zones V and VI comprised Telangana.
4. Hyderabad was included in Zone V.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Zones I to III were in Coastal Andhra, Zone IV was Rayalaseema, and Zones V and VI were in Telangana. Hyderabad was included in Zone VI, not Zone V.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed classification in an otherwise familiar regional grouping.
accepted.sec: Zonal system - list of zones and districts

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the zones of undivided Andhra Pradesh under the 1975 Order:

List-I (Zone)
a. Zone I
b. Zone II
c. Zone III
d. Zone IV

List-II (District group)
i. Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
ii. Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam
iii. Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
iv. East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Zone I consisted of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam; Zone II of East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone III of Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore; and Zone IV of Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure coastal pair and eliminate the codes with mismatched zone groups.
accepted.sec: Zonal system - list of zones and districts

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched under the zonal classification of undivided Andhra Pradesh?

1. Zone V — Adilabad, Karimnagar, Warangal and Khammam
2. Zone VI — Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy, Nizamabad, Mahbubnagar, Medak and Nalgonda
3. Zone IV — Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
4. Zone II — Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
accepted.x: The districts listed in statements 1 and 2 correctly belong to Zones V and VI respectively. Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore belonged to Zone III, while Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor belonged to Zone IV.
accepted.tq: Use the zone number to detect swapped district groups.
accepted.sec: Zonal system - list of zones and districts

accepted.s: After the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014, which zones of the undivided State were retained by Andhra Pradesh for its 13 districts?
accepted.x: After 2014, Andhra Pradesh retained Zones I to IV for its 13 districts; Zones V and VI related to the Telangana region.
accepted.tq: Test the boundary of the retained range rather than recalling an individual district.
accepted.sec: Zonal system - list of zones and districts

accepted.s:
With reference to the revised Andhra Pradesh Public Employment Order-2025, consider the following statements:
1. The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved six zones and two multi-zones.
2. The revised arrangement was approved in April 2026.
3. The Department of Personnel completed the final mapping in May 2026.
4. A multi-zone restricts candidates to posts available only within their own zone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Six zones and two multi-zones were approved in April 2026, and final mapping was completed in May 2026. A multi-zone enables candidates from adjacent zones to compete for a wider set of posts, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the practical effect of a multi-zone.
accepted.sec: Zonal system - list of zones and districts

accepted.s: The district-wise composition of the six new zones and two multi-zones for the 26 districts of Andhra Pradesh is presently:
o: Provided in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
Not available in the stated material
Identical to the six zones of undivided Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: The district list of Andhra Pradesh's six new zones and two multi-zones for its 26 districts is not provided in the stated material.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a stated structural fact from an unspecified detailed list.
accepted.sec: Zonal system - list of zones and districts

accepted.s: Which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided for Hyderabad to serve as the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
accepted.x: Section 5 provided for Hyderabad to be the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for the prescribed transitional period.
accepted.tq: Separate the section dealing with the common capital from the neighbouring sections on the Governor and security.
accepted.sec: Common capital Hyderabad - maximum period, Governor's responsibility

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

1. Section 5 — Common capital arrangement
2. Section 7 — One Governor for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
3. Section 8 — Governor's special responsibility in the common capital
4. Section 90 — Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: Section 90 declared Polavaram a national project. Special Category Status was an assurance made by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha and was not included in the Act.
accepted.tq: Use section-number association and isolate the option that substitutes an assurance for a statutory provision.
accepted.sec: Common capital Hyderabad - maximum period, Governor's responsibility

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 relating to the Polavaram submergence area primarily provided for:
o: Creation of seven new districts in Andhra Pradesh
Transfer of Polavaram administration to the Union Government
Transfer of seven mandals from Andhra Pradesh to Telangana
Transfer of seven mandals from Telangana to Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: The Ordinance amended Section 3 to transfer seven mandals, including Khammam villages in the submergence zone, from Telangana to Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Track the direction of territorial transfer instead of focusing only on the number of mandals.
accepted.sec: Polavaram national project, transfer of mandals, SCS, Ramapada Sagaram

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the original name of the Polavaram project is correct?
o: It was originally known as Polavaram Sagaram and was proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
It was originally known as Ramapada Sagaram and was proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
It was originally known as Ramapada Sagaram and was proposed by Arthur Cotton.
It was originally known as Godavari Sagaram and was proposed by K. L. Rao.
accepted.x: The original name was Ramapada Sagaram, and the proposal was associated with Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy. Arthur Cotton and K. L. Rao are incorrect attributions in this context.
accepted.tq: Separate the correct project name from the commonly substituted names of other engineers.
accepted.sec: Polavaram national project, transfer of mandals, SCS, Ramapada Sagaram

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position regarding Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh?
o: It was granted through the Polavaram Amendment Ordinance, 2014.
It was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha and was not included in the Act.
It was expressly enacted as a provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
It was recommended by the Srikrishna Committee in December 2010.
accepted.x: Special Category Status was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha, not a provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act. Andhra Pradesh has stated that the assurance was not fulfilled in full.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a political assurance from a statutory provision.
accepted.sec: Polavaram national project, transfer of mandals, SCS, Ramapada Sagaram

accepted.s: The 1969 agitation for Telangana was associated with which organisation and which date of Indira Gandhi's eight-point formula?
accepted.x: The 1969 agitation was associated with the Telangana Praja Samithi, and Indira Gandhi's eight-point formula is dated 11 April 1969.
accepted.tq: Link the movement organisation with its precise historical date.
accepted.sec: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the separate Telangana movement in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi
B. Centre's announcement after K. Chandrasekhar Rao's fast
C. Srikrishna Committee report
D. Million March
accepted.x: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in 2001, the Centre's announcement followed in December 2009, the Srikrishna Committee report came in December 2010, and the Million March occurred in March 2011.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence using the formation year first and the event months at the end.
accepted.sec: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme

accepted.s: Who founded the Telangana Rashtra Samithi, and in which year was it formed?
accepted.x: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in 2001 by K. Chandrasekhar Rao.
accepted.tq: Match the movement organisation with its founder and formation year.
accepted.sec: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme

accepted.s: The Centre's announcement following K. Chandrasekhar Rao's fast for Telangana was made in:
accepted.x: The Centre made the relevant announcement in December 2009 after K. Chandrasekhar Rao's fast.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the announcement date from the later committee and resolution dates.
accepted.sec: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

1. Srikrishna Committee report — December 2010
2. Million March at Tank Bund — March 2011
3. Sakala Janula Samme — September–October 2011
4. Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana — July 2013
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct: the Srikrishna Committee report was issued in December 2010, the Million March occurred at Tank Bund in March 2011, Sakala Janula Samme took place during September–October 2011, and the CWC resolution came in July 2013.
accepted.tq: Confirm each event-date pair before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme

accepted.s: Sakala Janula Samme, associated with the separate Telangana movement, was:
o: An eight-point formula announced in April 1969
A parliamentary resolution adopted in July 2013
A one-day march at Tank Bund during March 2011
A general strike lasting approximately 42 days during September–October 2011
accepted.x: Sakala Janula Samme was a general strike that lasted approximately 42 days during September–October 2011. The Tank Bund march was the Million March, held in March 2011.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the prolonged general strike from the one-day Million March.
accepted.sec: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme

accepted.s: The Million March associated with the Telangana movement was held at Tank Bund in:
accepted.x: The Million March was held at Tank Bund in March 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the location as the anchor and distinguish its date from the neighbouring movement events.
accepted.sec: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme

accepted.s:
Which event occurred latest among the following?

A. Formation of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi
B. Srikrishna Committee report
C. Sakala Janula Samme
D. Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana
accepted.x: The Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana was adopted in July 2013, later than the TRS formation in 2001, the Srikrishna Committee report in 2010 and Sakala Janula Samme in 2011.
accepted.tq: Identify the latest event by comparing the years before comparing the months.
accepted.sec: Separate Telangana movement - TRS, Srikrishna Committee, Million March, Sakala Janula Samme
